prereg_text:
U5 pre-registration (written 2026-10-10 BEFORE any orbit run; not to be moved afterwards)

DESIGN CRITERION (design_synthesis.json, U5, unchanged):
  Engine pass iff ratio (C-A)/(B-A) = 0.0527 +/- 0.003, i.e. in [0.0497, 0.0557].
  Physics: sigma hook excluded iff Delta-omega_sigma = (C-A) > 0.05 arcsec/cy. Predicted ~2.3 arcsec/cy.
  Runs: 50 orbits, Forest-Ruth, dt = 600 s. A Newtonian; B include_gr=True; C Sun.sigma = XI*r_s/r updated every step.

ESTIMATOR (fixed before running):
  Primary  = direction of the osculating Laplace-Runge-Lenz vector (relative coords, mu = G(M_sun+M_mer), unscaled)
             evaluated at each discrete radial-minimum step; linear fit vs orbit index -> advance per orbit.
             Reason: the sketch's atan2(position) at the discrete minimum carries a timing term Omega_p*(t_sample - t_peri)
             that does not cancel in C-A once the anomalistic period changes (estimated ~1e-7 rad/orbit vs signal 2.6e-8).
  Secondary (reported, not used for pass/fail) = the sketch's own estimator verbatim, and parabola-interpolated
             position angle at the r minimum.

ADDED PREDICTIONS FROM READING THE CODE (made before running):
  P1  nbody.py gr_1pn branch (lines ~463-477) adds +factor*[(4GM/r - v^2) r_hat + 4 (r_hat.v) v] with r_hat pointing
      FROM Mercury TO the Sun. The standard harmonic-gauge 1PN test-body EOM is +(GM/c^2 r^3)[(4GM/r - v^2) x + 4 (x.v) v]
      with x pointing from the Sun to Mercury. The engine term is the overall NEGATIVE of the standard one.
      => predicted B-A = -1.00 x Delta-omega_GR (retrograde, about -43 arcsec/cy), so the design ratio (C-A)/(B-A) comes
      out about -0.0527 and the design's engine criterion FAILS on the GR run's sign, not on the sigma hook.
      Force-level probe: cos(angle) between engine a_1PN and the standard a_1PN at perihelion predicted = -1.
  Corrected criterion (reported alongside the original): (C-A)/Delta-omega_GR,analytic in [0.0497, 0.0557], with
      Delta-omega_GR,analytic = 6 pi G M /(c^2 a (1-e^2)) evaluated by Mentat simplify_expr; and |B-A|/Delta-omega_GR,analytic
      in [0.99, 1.01] with its sign recorded.
  P2  add-on run D, sigma = sigma_from_potential(r, M_sun) = XI*r_s/(2r) (the inventory normalisation):
      (D-A)/Delta-omega_GR,analytic = XI/6 = 0.02637 +/- 0.0015.
  P3  add-on run E, toggles eih_cross=True: radial terms carry the standard sign, the velocity cross term
      (vec_ij.(4v_i-3v_j))(v_i-v_j) carries the opposite sign of Moyer/Will (they use x_i - x_j). Coefficient bookkeeping
      Delta-omega = (pi m/p)(-A_coef - 2 B_coef + 2 D_coef) with A=4, B=-1, D=-4 gives -10 pi m/p = -(5/3) Delta-omega_GR.
      Predicted (E-A)/Delta-omega_GR,analytic = -1.667 +/- 0.03.
  P4  dt-halving control (A and C at dt = 300 s): (C-A) changes by < 1 %.
provenance_note: Every block in this JSON is written by u5_aggregate_v2.py from leaves_v2.json, runs_v2/, probe_v2.json and PREREG.txt. In v1, design_corrections, coupling_convention_record, engine_defects, prereg_text and lit_refs were added to u5_results.json by hand after u5_aggregate.py ran; v2 removes that gap.

sun.source: sigma-ground via IAU 2015 nominal solar values

mercury.source: sigma-ground via NASA Planetary Fact Sheet 2024

e_mercury.source: [LIT] NASA NSSDC Mercury Fact Sheet, nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/mercuryfact.html (orbital eccentricity 0.2056; re-fetched 2026-10-10 in the v2 repair, also a = 57.909e6 km, P = 87.969 d)

XI.source: sigma_ground.inventory.core.sigma.XI = 0.1582 (repo constant). NOTE: the docstring at sigma.py:40 attributes it to Planck 2018 Omega_b h^2 = 0.02237, Omega_c h^2 = 0.1200, but those numbers give 0.1571 (see leaf xi_docstring_check); 0.1582 is used here as the repo constant, not as a Planck value.

will2014_beta_bound.source: [LIT] Will 2014, Living Rev. Relativ. 17, 4 (arXiv:1403.7377), Table 4: beta-1 < 8e-5 (perihelion shift, J2 = (2.2 +/- 0.1)e-7); text after eq. 65: beta-1 = (-4.1 +/- 7.8)e-5 (MESSENGER fits, Cassini gamma adopted). Read from the arXiv PDF in the v2 repair.

will2006_2g_b_1_bound.source: [LIT] Will 2006, Living Rev. Relativ. 9, 3 (gr-qc/0510072), text after eq. 50: excess perihelion shift known to about 0.1 percent from radar observations of Mercury 1966-1990, giving |2 gamma - beta - 1| < 3e-3. Read from the arXiv PDF in the v2 repair.

park2017_beta_central.source: [LIT] Park, Folkner, Konopliv, Williams, Smith, Zuber 2017, AJ 153, 121, doi:10.3847/1538-3881/aa5be2: beta-1 = (-2.7 +/- 3.9)e-5 (verified by the v1 runner via MIT DSpace and by two skeptics; the v2 repair could not re-fetch it: publisher bot-check, ADS 405, web-search budget exhausted)

will_GR_arcsec_cy.source: [LIT] Will 2014 eq. 65 / Will 2006 eq. 50: 42.98 arcsec/cy for gamma = beta = 1

design_budget_arcsec_cy.source: design's own conservative budget (U5 design entry); ~0.1 % of 42.98 arcsec/cy, i.e. the Will 2006 radar level

headline: With σ = ξ r_s/r imposed by the U5 harness on the Sun at every step (a long-range field; the engine itself only carries a constant per-body σ), nbody's e^σ GM scaling advances Mercury's perihelion by 0.0527335 ± 2.2e-07 of GR. That matches ξ/3 to 2.3e-06 relative (0.55 SE), and an orbit-averaged Gauss quadrature on the engine forces gives 0.05273332. The advance is 2.267″/cy: 45× the design's conservative 0.05″/cy budget and ~1978× Will 2014's β bound, so this coupling is excluded. That result was [DERIVED] from the fixed ξ before the run; the engine run confirms it. The design's own engine criterion fails (ratio -0.0527) because the engine's gr_1pn term has the wrong overall sign: the 1PN run precesses at -42.99″/cy (-1.0000035 × GR). eih_cross runs at -1.6667 × GR (velocity term flipped). The 2PN static term's sign is correct.
could_it_fail: The Mercury exclusion itself could not fail in this run. ξ = 0.1582 is a fixed repo constant, and Binet's ξ/3 × 42.98″/cy ≈ 2.3″/cy was written into the design before the run. The exclusion is therefore [DERIVED] (Binet series and ξ/3 by Mentat) against [LIT] bounds, and the 50-orbit run is [VERIFIED numerics] confirmation. The run could only have changed the verdict by showing that the engine fails to apply its own e^σ scaling, which would be an engine defect, not the hook surviving. Three things could genuinely fail. (i) The engine reproducing ξ/3: a wrong derivation (the designs' earlier 2ξ/3), a hook on the wrong body, or σ lagging inside the Forest–Ruth step would each have shown. It landed 2.3e-06 relative (0.55 fit SE) from ξ/3, and the integrator-free Gauss quadrature on the same engine forces gives ξ/3 to 1.6e-07. (ii) The two 1PN sign predictions, pre-registered from code reading in PREREG.txt (−1 and −5/3 × GR). Both came out (-1.0000035, -1.6666675), and the off-perihelion force probe fixes each term's sign separately. (iii) The dt-halving control (-4.0e-06). The design's engine criterion did fail, as predicted. ξ/3 itself is [BY CONSTRUCTION] for any e^σ-scaled force with σ ∝ 1/r.
evidential_weight: Against one specific object: nbody's e^σ scaling of the source's GM, driven by a harness-imposed σ = ξ r_s/r_Mercury with no range cutoff (λ → ∞). The engine has no σ(r) of its own; it carries a constant per-body sigma_field (nbody.py:199, 233), and this prescription is undefined for N > 2 bodies. As a long-range coupling it is excluded [DERIVED + LIT, confirmed by engine]: 45.3× the design's conservative 0.05″/cy budget, ~1978× Will 2014's β−1 < 8e-5, and ~4056 σ from Park+2017's β. The ξ r_s/2r amplitude, applied through the same source-GM coupling, is excluded at 23× (~989× Will 2014). This is an exclusion by an independent observable, but with the same ansatz and the same ξ as the program's S9a. It is much weaker than S9a's 10^5 (clocks) to 10^11 (free fall), and comparable to the §14 PPN battery (Cassini ×10^4, lunar ranging ×10^3.6). Under the Captain's ξ bet the program already limits σ's range to below ~35 km (§6), where this hook is zero at Mercury. It adds nothing for the unification thesis: any 1/r³ force of this amplitude fails the same way. The significant side result is for the repo. Both nbody 1PN paths run Mercury's perihelion backwards: gr_1pn at −1 × GR, with both terms flipped, and eih_cross at −5/3 × GR, with the velocity term flipped. So every include_gr=True, gr_1pn or eih_cross result from this engine carries the wrong relativistic correction, and no test in the suite can see it.
design_corrections: The design's engine criterion divides by the engine's own GR run (B−A). That run is retrograde (-1.0000035 × GR) because of the gr_1pn sign defect, so the design ratio is -0.0527333 ± 2.4e-07 and the criterion FAILS for a reason unrelated to the σ hook. The corrected criterion, pre-registered in PREREG.txt, measures (C−A) against the analytic GR advance 6πGM/(c²a(1−e²)) evaluated by Mentat. Result: 0.0527335, PASS. Against the original criterion: FAIL.

The design sketch's perihelion estimator (atan2 of the position one step after the discrete radial minimum) has 2.2e-04 rad rms sampling jitter per orbit (fit residual, run C), four orders above the σ signal of 2.6e-08 rad/orbit. As written it returns a ratio of 0.171 and C/GR = -1.56, which is noise. Before running it was replaced with the osculating Laplace–Runge–Lenz direction at the radial minimum (fit residual rms 1.1e-11 rad). The parabola-interpolated angle agrees to 2.9e-06 relative for C−A (1.6e-06 for B−A, 2.4e-06 for D−A).

The repo has two σ amplitudes. The field equation gives ξ r_s/r, so ξ/3; inventory sigma_from_potential gives ξ GM/(rc²) = ξ r_s/2r, so ξ/6. Both were run through nbody's source-GM e^σ coupling, and both are excluded in that coupling. Run D is NOT a test of the inventory's own coupling (σ scaling 0.99 of the TEST body's mass). Under that coupling, a pure static gradient force −∇(f m c² σ) with constant inertial mass is a 1/r² force that only renormalises GM, with no first-order perihelion advance [DERIVED]. If σ also changes the inertial mass (a σ-dependent mass in the point-particle action), velocity-dependent terms of 1PN order appear, of the form f ξ GM/(c²r²)(r̂·v)v [DERIVED, structural, not evaluated], and Mercury would be sensitive. Neither variant is tested here; the program's S9a battery addresses that convention.

The design predicted '~2 orders' of exclusion. Against the design's own 0.05″/cy budget it is 1.66 orders (45.3×). That budget is conservative: it is about 0.1 % of 42.98″/cy, the radar-era accuracy that Will 2006 quotes. Against Will 2014's β−1 < 8e-5 the hook is ~1978× over the allowed 1.15e-03″/cy. Against Park+2017 it is 4056 σ, where the 1σ is 5.59e-04″/cy.

Framing: the σ(r) = ξ r_s/r prescription belongs to the U5 harness (u5_run.py sets Sun.sigma_field every step from Mercury's distance), not to the engine. The excluded object is that harness-driven, long-range e^σ GM hook.

The design treated the physics verdict as something the run could decide. It could not: with ξ fixed, the exclusion follows from Binet's ξ/3 before any run. The run tests the engine, not the hook's survival.
coupling_convention_record: nbody.CelestialBody.gm_m3_s2 (nbody.py:225-233) multiplies the SOURCE body's whole GM by e^σ. With σ set from the test body's distance (by the harness), this is a universal, attractive 1/r³ addition, and it is not reciprocal: the Sun does not feel a scaled Mercury. inventory.core.sigma scales only the QCD part (0.99) of the TEST body's mass. sigma_from_potential uses ξ GM/(rc²) = ξ r_s/2r, while the field equation gives ξ r_s/r. Three conventions, two amplitudes. If σ were the Sun's own (constant) value, the hook would be a constant GM rescaling with no precession.

engine_defects.defect: The gr_1pn branch (lines 472-477) has the overall wrong sign. It adds +GM/(r²c²)[(4GM/r − v²) r̂ + 4(r̂·v)v] with r̂ = r_ij/r, and r_ij = x_source − x_body is defined at line 406. That is the negative of IERS Conventions eq. 10.12, GM/(c²r³)[(4GM/r − v²)r + 4(r·v)v], where r runs from the central body to the orbiter. Both the radial and the velocity term are flipped.
engine_defects.evidence: Force probe fitted at true anomalies 0, π/2, 2 and 4 rad, against the IERS pieces: radial coefficient -1.0000000001, velocity coefficient -0.9999999999 (fit residual 2.1e-10). At perihelion x·v = 0, so v1's perihelion-only probe (cos = −1.000) tested only the radial term. At f = π/2, where x·v/(rv) = 0.201, |engine + IERS|/|IERS| = 5.7e-12. Static probe: the engine coefficient is -4.000000 × x·GM/r², against +4 from harmonic Schwarzschild (Mentat series −1 + 4x − 9x²). Gauss quadrature on the engine force gives -1.0000001 × GR. The 50-orbit run gives B−A = -42.991″/cy = -1.0000035 × GR, against +42.98″/cy [LIT, Will 2014]. This was predicted from code reading in PREREG.txt before the run. Suite blindness: test_physics_stability.py:215, test_mercury_precesses_with_gr_on, asserts only delta_au > 0 (line 237). test_nbody.py:1587 compares |a_eih|/|a_1pn| to 1 within 1e-4 (line 1617), about 1e4 coarser than the ~1e-8 1PN term. Callers that enable it: rolling_shootout.py:245-247, scripts/run_long_horizon_sweep.py:267, scripts/run_toggle_iteration.py:39, test_future_predictions.py:222, test_probe_propagation.py:177 and 183, test_shootout.py:245, and test_physics_stability.py:71, 225 and 454. Not patched (Mentat flags, never fixes).

engine_defects.defect: In the eih_cross branch, the velocity cross term (r_ij·(4v_i − 3v_j))(v_i − v_j) at lines 457-459 uses r_ij = x_j − x_i (defined at line 406). The EIH/Moyer form uses x_i − x_j there. The radial A_ij terms (lines 446-455) carry the correct sign.
engine_defects.evidence: Force probe against the IERS pieces: radial coefficient 1.0000004, velocity coefficient -1.0000001. At f = π/2, cos(engine, IERS) = 0.856, and the residual against IERS with the cross term flipped is 4.0e-07. Static radial coefficient 4.000002 (correct, +4). Gauss quadrature gives -1.6666669 × GR. The 50-orbit run gives E−A = -71.652″/cy = -1.6666675 × GR, matching the pre-registered bookkeeping (πm/p)(−A − 2B + 2D) with D = −4 (Mentat: −5/3). A correct EIH gives +1. The docstring calls this branch the 'canonical force model used by JPL DE440'.

engine_defects.defect: Documentation and provenance only: the XI docstring (and line 25) attributes ξ = 0.1582 to Planck 2018 Ω_b h² = 0.02237, Ω_c h² = 0.1200, but those numbers give ξ = 0.1571.
engine_defects.evidence: Mentat simplify_expr 0.02237/(0.02237+0.1200) = 0.157126. With that ξ, the hook would be 2.252″/cy instead of 2.267″/cy (45.0× the budget), so no conclusion changes. misc/UNIFICATION_PROGRAM.md:317 already carries both values ('0.1571 / 0.1582'). Not patched.

resolved_not_defective: The gr_2pn leading term (nbody.py:504-509) has the correct sign. Static probe: engine coefficient -9.000000, -9.000000 and -9.000000 × x²·GM/r² at x = 1e-4, 1e-3 and 1e-2 (outward positive). Harmonic-gauge static Schwarzschild gives a_r/(GM/r²) = −1 + 4x − 9x² (Mentat differentiate_expr, simplify_expr and series_expansion from g00 = −(r−m)/(r+m), g_rr = (r+m)/(r−m)). The +4 reproduces IERS 2(β+γ) = 4, which checks the gauge, and the −9 is inward like the engine's term. Only the static piece was tested; the docstring says the velocity-dependent 2PN terms are absent.
lit_refs: NASA NSSDC Mercury Fact Sheet, nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/mercuryfact.html: e = 0.2056, a = 57.909e6 km, sidereal period 87.969 d (re-fetched in the v2 repair).

Will 2014, Living Rev. Relativ. 17, 4, arXiv:1403.7377, §4.2: eq. 65, 42.98″/cy × [(2+2γ−β)/3 + 3e-4 J2/1e-7]; MESSENGER-era fits with Cassini γ give β−1 = (−4.1 ± 7.8)e-5; Table 4 lists β−1 < 8e-5 from the perihelion shift. Read from the arXiv PDF in the v2 repair.

Will 2006, Living Rev. Relativ. 9, 3, arXiv:gr-qc/0510072, text after eq. 50: Mercury's excess perihelion shift known to about 0.1 % from radar observations (1966–1990), giving |2γ − β − 1| < 3e-3. This, not Will 2014, is the source of the radar statement v1 attributed to Will 2014. Read from the arXiv PDF in the v2 repair.

Park, Folkner, Konopliv, Williams, Smith, Zuber 2017, AJ 153, 121, doi:10.3847/1538-3881/aa5be2: β−1 = (−2.7 ± 3.9)e-5, J2 = (2.25 ± 0.09)e-7, total precession 575.3100 ± 0.0015″/cy. Verified by the v1 runner (MIT DSpace) and two skeptics; the v2 repair could not re-fetch it (publisher bot-check, ADS 405, search budget exhausted).

U. Hugentobler 2008, 'Orbit Perturbations due to Relativistic Corrections' (citing IERS Conventions 2003): Schwarzschild term GM/(c²r³){[2(β+γ)GM/r − γv²]r + 2(1+γ)(r·v)v} with r from the central body, a constant outward radial acceleration for a circular orbit, and the Gauss equation for ω̇ (eq. 6) used in u5_probe_v2.py. Text read from the PDF in lit_pdf/.
caveats: Mercury's eccentricity 0.2056 is typed as [LIT] (NSSDC, re-fetched) because Mentat's solar_system_body has no eccentricity field. The ratio ξ/3 does not depend on e; only the ″/cy values do.

Mentat's M_sun of 1.98892e30 kg (labelled IAU 2015 nominal) is ~2.6e-4 above GM_sun/G, so the analytic GR comes out 42.991″/cy rather than 42.98. The ″/cy conversion uses the catalogue sidereal period of 87.969 d. The simulated orbit's anomalistic period is 87.9577 d, which is 1.3e-04 different. Converted with the simulated period, the hook is 2.2674″/cy instead of 2.2671″/cy. No ratio is affected.

Precision: the C ratio's fit SE is 2.2e-07 absolute (4.2e-06 relative), so the ξ/3 deviation of 2.3e-06 is 0.55 SE. Run vs Gauss quadrature differs by +3.4 ppm (B), +2.5 (C), +2.1 (D), +0.4 (E) and -1.6 (C at dt 300). That is consistent with the -4.0 ppm dt-halving shift: a few-ppm integration and estimator systematic, immaterial to every conclusion.
σ is set on the Sun once per Forest–Ruth step, from the start-of-step distance. The dt-halving control shows this is irrelevant at the ppm level.
With σ on, momentum is not conserved: Mercury feels the Sun's GM × e^σ, but the Sun feels Mercury's unscaled GM. This is negligible at a mass ratio of 1.7e-7, and it is a property of the hook.

The Park+2017 and Will 2014 comparisons treat the hook as a pure PPN β shift of −ξ [DERIVED: an extra inward 2ξ(GM)²/(c²r³)]. Park's β bound assumes Cassini's γ and fits J2 jointly, so the σ figures are indicative. The headline factor uses the design's conservative 0.05″/cy budget.
This is a two-body Sun–Mercury run with no planetary perturbations, no J2 and no 2PN. The comparison is differential (C−A), so those terms do not enter the ratio.

The harmonic radius r = R − m used for the 2PN sign check is the standard textbook identification. It was not web-verified in this repair (search budget exhausted); its 1PN coefficient reproduces the verified IERS 2(β+γ) = 4.
No engine code was changed. The 1PN sign defects need a Captain decision, a fix, and a quantitative perihelion test (for example B−A = +42.98 ± 0.1″/cy with the LRL estimator in u5_run.py).

ACCEPTED (skeptic 3): could_it_fail is rewritten. The exclusion is [DERIVED] and was known before the run.

ACCEPTED (skeptic 3): 'fourth independent exclusion' becomes 'independent observable, same ansatz and ξ, much weaker than S9a'.

PARTLY ACCEPTED (skeptic 3, run D): run D is qualified as a test of the source-GM coupling only. Not adopted unconditionally: 'Mercury does not test the inventory convention'. That holds for a pure static gradient force with constant inertial mass, but if σ also changes the inertial mass, 1PN-order velocity terms appear. Both variants are now stated, and neither is tested here.

REJECTED (skeptic 3): 'the 2.3e-6 deviation is ~10× the fit SE'. The fit SE in GR-ratio units is 2.2e-07 absolute = 4.2e-06 relative, so the deviation is 0.55 SE (skeptic 1's reading). The run-vs-Gauss differences, a few ppm, match the dt-control shift, and that is how they are now described.
